The estate can collect damages for the injuries caused by the driver’s negligence, including pain and suffering and any losses up to the point of death, but generally not for the death itself if the refusal of treatment is deemed an independent, superseding cause of death. Under the common law “eggshell plaintiff” rule, the driver is liable for the pedestrian’s pre-existing condition (here, her religious refusal), but many jurisdictions treat an unreasonable refusal of life-saving treatment as a break in causation, limiting recovery to non-death damages.
